steps.text: Open Build with my agent. In the actual Workbench setup, choose the diagram detail that matches the audience: Story, Mixed, or Engineering. The source-path examples below are separate from this audience setting.
Select Story in the actual Workbench detail selector for the business story example. Story focus keeps the PM narrative in people, actions, and outcomes; an engineer can enrich the same folder later.
Select Engineering for this HLD walkthrough. Detail level serves the audience; the HLD is independent source material chosen in this tour.
Select Engineering for this trace walkthrough. Detail level serves the audience; the Honeycomb export is independent source material chosen in this tour.
With Story detail selected, find Copy & paste in the full Workbench dialog. The orange outline marks the next control.
With Engineering detail selected, find Copy & paste in the full Workbench dialog. The orange outline marks the next control.
Select the focused Copy & paste control for an external Claude Code conversation. The three source paths are choices in this tour, not buttons in the Workbench.
Select an empty diagram folder. Flowview prepares the spec, coverage ledger, and connection instructions in that folder.
Copy the setup instructions into Claude Code. The exchange below is illustrative, not a captured transcript.

log.text: [Pasted Flowview Setup Instructions]
I can read this folder. What is your source, who will view the diagram, and which outcome should the story explain?

steps.text: Business story: a PM explains the resident journey in plain language; Story detail keeps technical gaps visible rather than guessing them.

log.text: Audience: product and engineering. A visitor presses the doorbell; the resident should receive an alert. Show the major handoffs without service names yet.
Does the story include an actual clip playback, or only a recording request and notification? What is the starting state?

steps.text: The PM clarifies the outcome and boundary. Claude can now storyboard six beats, leaving backend identities for the engineer.

log.text: Start with a quiet porch. Show the press, recording request, stored clip metadata, queued alert, then resident notification. Do not claim playback or a failure.
I will draft those six beats as a story and mark service identities, protocols, and delivery evidence as engineer handoff questions.

steps.text: Claude names the six doorbell beats and explicitly marks the technical enrichment still needed.

log.text: Draft: 1 quiet; 2 button event reaches hub; 3 recording requested; 4 clip metadata stored; 5 notification queued; 6 resident alert sent. The PM version uses plain boxes; engineering names and evidence come later.
Keep that order. The engineer can enrich the same folder and ledger after reviewing actual design and trace evidence.

steps.text: HLD design: an engineer supplies the proposed architecture. Claude distinguishes design intent from verified runtime behavior.

log.text: Use the fictional doorbell HLD: porch hub receives the button event; recording service requests a recording, writes metadata, and queues a resident alert.
Does the HLD specify the last delivery hop? Which outcomes are design intent rather than observed production behavior?

steps.text: The engineer names the remaining proposed hop and scopes the claim.

log.text: Notification service delivers to the resident app. This is proposed design, not production proof. Keep the starting quiet state and no playback or failure claim.
I will label the diagram as authored HLD, show the six planned beats, and keep acceptance and operational validation as separate decisions.

steps.text: Claude records the HLD decisions and unanswered questions beside the six-step proposal.

log.text: Draft: quiet → button received → recording requested → metadata persisted → alert queued → resident notified. The ledger marks route/ownership decisions as HLD source and flags any missing evidence.
That is the story to review. Do not present this design as a measured trace.

steps.text: Honeycomb trace: an engineer brings an export and investigation question. The observed spans do not themselves prove every customer-facing beat.

log.text: Use the fictional happy trace. Which doorbell hops are observed, and which part of the six-step diagram is authored context?

I see porch-hub POST /button, recording-service POST /recordings, clip-store INSERT clip, notification-queue publish doorbell, and notification-service POST /notifications. I will check their parent or link relationships.

steps.text: Claude separates trace observations from inferred or authored context before drawing an edge.

log.text: Show the trace-backed service chain. Keep quiet porch, physical button press, and resident-app notification labeled as authored context unless another source supports them.
The trace has five spans and a queue-to-notification link. It does not by itself prove the camera event, app receipt, playback, or a failure. I will not infer those as observations.

steps.text: The same six-beat diagram gains evidence annotations only where the Honeycomb export supports them.

log.text: Draft: six canonical beats. Spans support hub, recording request, metadata insert, queue publish, and notification-service call. The ledger separates those observations from HLD/customer-outcome assertions.
Good. Show the evidence gaps in preview so I can decide whether the authored context is acceptable.

steps.text: Claude writes the draft Flowview spec and coverage ledger in the selected folder, then asks for a human preview. This is a proposal, not automatic approval.

log.text: The candidate spec and ledger are ready in the folder. Please inspect the visual steps and evidence notes in Flowview before committing the update.

steps.text: Open Review and accept, then choose First creation. Its source-neutral Workbench fixture illustrates a representative first candidate from an empty folder after whichever starting material shaped the draft; it does not claim to capture this illustrative Claude exchange.

sections.heading: Update a saved doorbell diagram with Claude
text: Alternative entry: this diagram folder already has an accepted spec and coverage ledger. Reopen it, read the current pair, then request an update. An existing flow can be presented to Story, Mixed, or Engineering audiences.

panels.title: Illustrative Claude Code continuation · YOU / CLAUDE

steps.text: Alternative entry: open Agent beside the existing doorbell diagram. The disconnected panel offers Reopen diagram folder; this is not a new empty-folder build.
Click Reopen diagram folder. The focused actual Workbench control names the saved doorbell project and notes that interrupted requests will not replay.
Choose Continue an existing agent build, then Select Diagram Folder. This reopens the saved folder; a new build would require an empty folder.
Select the same folder. Flowview reads its accepted spec and ledger and restores Workbench history; old pending requests and native Claude chat are not replayed.
Review and copy the fresh setup for this folder. Copy & paste keeps the conversation in Claude Code; the Workbench shows the current project filenames.
Paste the current setup into Claude Code. This illustrative exchange starts a new conversation with the saved project, not inherited chat memory.

log.text: [Pasted Flowview Setup Instructions]
I will verify this folder, then read the current accepted spec and ledger. A new Claude session does not inherit the earlier conversation.

steps.text: Claude inventories the accepted spec and ledger before editing. The person names the audience and intended direction here; the formal change request is copied in the next step.

log.text: I found the six-step doorbell diagram and its ledger. The accepted story ends at the resident alert; I will preserve its stable step IDs and existing service route.
The audience is product leadership. I want the resident-facing story clearer; first confirm the existing six steps, engineering Data flow, and ledger that the formal request must preserve.

steps.text: In Agent → Copy & paste, use Copy request and paste the registered instruction into Claude Code. This is the formal change request; copying it alone does not send it.

log.text: Formal request: rewrite only the resident-facing step wording for product leaders. Preserve all six step IDs, the engineering Data flow, and the coverage ledger without source or evidence edits.
I will compare the seeded candidate with the accepted files, then change only the requested step wording. The coverage ledger will remain unchanged in this first proposal.

steps.text: Claude asks how to present the existing flow to business readers while preserving its engineering view and stable steps.

log.text: Should the resident-facing Story replace the engineering Data flow, or sit beside it with the same six steps?
Keep both. Lead with what the resident experiences, preserve the service route and six stable step IDs, and do not add playback or failure.

steps.text: Claude changes only resident-facing step wording in the first candidate spec and leaves the coverage ledger unchanged. Workbench presents that wording-only proposal for human preview; the accepted folder pair stays unchanged until approval.

log.text: The first candidate makes the resident story clearer while retaining the existing Data flow and six step IDs. I left the coverage ledger unchanged.
I validated the wording-only candidate and submitted it for Flowview preview. Please inspect step 6 and the unchanged ledger before deciding.

steps.text: Open Review and accept, then choose Update existing. Preview the wording-only candidate against the saved Current spec and ledger; a later evidence correction must be reviewed as a fresh proposal.

sections.heading: Review the first proposal or an existing update
text: Choose First creation for an empty-folder build, or Update existing for a revision to an accepted diagram. Each path shows the actual Workbench preview and ends with human approval; repository publication remains separate.

steps.text: First creation: this actual Workbench preview shows a representative source-neutral doorbell candidate from an empty folder. It illustrates the human gate after any Build new starting path; Proposed state is selected, with no accepted six-step baseline yet.
Click Current state. The folder still contains the empty My story scaffold with zero nodes; it has no accepted six-step doorbell diagram to compare against.
Return to Proposed state and inspect step 1 of 6. Play through the proposed quiet porch → hub → recording → clip store → notification queue → notification service sequence before deciding.
Expand Coverage ledger for the first candidate. Check its six proposed beats, source-check warning, and required human review before accepting either file.
Click Commit update after reviewing the first candidate and ledger. Flowview saves both in the diagram folder; the applied receipt and Undo confirm local acceptance.
The first accepted spec and ledger are local files. Company repository review publishes them separately before Backstage can read the approved snapshot.
Continue to Find and use in Backstage to see how an explicitly bound, published diagram appears on a service page.
Update existing begins with the wording-only candidate from Reconnect. Preview Agent Updates opens on Proposed state: one item modified, accepted ledger unchanged, and no update committed yet.

Inspect Proposed step 6. The clearer resident wording now says the app receives an alert without marking that app outcome as authored context; the evidence boundary needs explicit treatment before approval.
Click Current state to compare the accepted six-step baseline. Its existing step 6 says the notification service delivers an alert to the resident app; this baseline has a saved coverage ledger.

Expand Coverage ledger in Current state. The accepted ledger already distinguishes the authored HLD app outcome from a trace that ends at notification-service; use it to review the unqualified first proposal.

Return to Proposed state and click Discard update on the first wording-only proposal. Workbench records Not applied; the accepted spec and ledger remain unchanged while Claude prepares a corrected candidate.

Explain why the first step-6 wording needs a source boundary: the accepted ledger limits trace evidence to the notification-service call, while app delivery remains authored design. Ask Claude to revise the candidate spec and ledger and submit a fresh preview.
Claude submits a fresh candidate spec and ledger after the feedback. Preview Agent Updates opens a second proposal; compare it anew before committing.
Click Current state in the second proposal. The first wording candidate was discarded, so this is still the same accepted baseline and not a partly accepted draft.
Click Proposed state and inspect step 6. It now labels the resident-app alert as fictional authored design and says the trace only reaches the notification-service call; app receipt is unobserved.

Inspect the focused changed Coverage ledger. It repeats the authored outcome and trace limit and flags the revised business wording for human review. Compare it with the spec before accepting both files.

Click Commit update only after comparing the second proposal. Flowview saves its corrected spec and ledger together in the folder; the Applied receipt and Undo confirm local acceptance. This is not a Git commit.
Workbench acceptance saves this update locally. Separate company repository review publishes the changed pair before Backstage reads it; this process hop is conceptual.
Continue to Find and use in Backstage after separate repository publication of the accepted update.

sections.heading: Walk the Recording service Diagrams preview
text: This local host shows the actual Flowview plugin with fictional catalog data. Follow its selected doorbell diagram through the inline viewer, service jumps, expanded canvas, and return to the entity.

steps.text: We arrive on the Recording service Diagrams surface. Its explicit binding reveals one associated fictional doorbell spec in this fixture.
The Diagram selector contains that one associated spec. Click Data flow inside the selected diagram: the native inline viewer changes from the Home scene to the service graph.
Scroll below the inline viewer and open Where this service appears. It reveals the matching doorbell section and three Recording service step links.
Click Doorbell press to resident notification. The selected diagram jumps to that section and shows its opening step, A quiet home.
Click the step 3 link, Recording service accepts the request. The inline viewer moves to STEP 3/6 and shows its recording-workflow caption.
Click Expand canvas. The viewer fills the window; the floating controls still show STEP 3/6 and the recording-workflow caption. Use Back to entity to return.
Click Back to entity. The expanded view closes and the Recording service Diagrams surface returns with the same selected spec.
